title: Work that does not move forward
literal_meaning: The swollen-legged person digs; as much as they dig, so much they tread over.
explanation: The image suggests effort whose result is undone as the work proceeds. It can be used for a task that stays unfinished because each advance is cancelled by another action. Its bodily caricature should be recognized rather than turned into a judgment about disabled people.
meaning_odia: ଏକ ପଟେ କାମ ଆଗଉଛି, ଅନ୍ୟ ପଟେ ସେହି କାମ ପୁଣି ନଷ୍ଟ ହେଉଛି—ଏହି ଅସଂଗତିକୁ କଥାଟି ଧରେ। କରିଥିବା ପରିଶ୍ରମର ଫଳ ନିଜ ବା ଅନ୍ୟର କାମରେ ମାଟି ହୋଇଗଲେ ଏହି ଭାବ ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ପୁରୁଣା ଉପମାରେ ଶାରୀରିକ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ଉଲ୍ଲେଖ ଥିଲେ ବି ମଣିଷର ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ବିଷୟରେ ସେଥିରୁ ସାଧାରଣ ନିଷ୍କର୍ଷ ଟାଣିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: A document is repeatedly reformatted, and each revision removes changes that the team had already agreed on. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Godara is rendered as the saying’s description of swollen legs, without diagnosing a medical condition. The interpretation concerns self-defeating work, not physical capacity or personal worth. The figurative explanation is an editorial interpretation, not a separately verified traditional gloss.
